newsitem.title: UK: Dlr boosted as US strikes Iraq but reaction muted.
newsitem.headline: Dlr boosted as US strikes Iraq but reaction muted.

text.p: The dollar received a boost from news the U.S. had launched a Cruise missile attack on air defense targets in Iraq, but the dollar's initial reaction was fairly muted. "The difference this time around is that the air strikes have come at the start of European forex day," said Nick Parsons, forex strategist at Banque Paribas in Paris. "Desert Storm was launched in the middle of the night so everyone had time to think about it and come in buy dollars so there was quite a lot of momentum behind the dollar last time."
The dollar touched a peak of around 1.4912 marks and 109.35 in the wake of the raid on Iraq, not too far from Monday's European closings of 1.4863/70 and 109.10/18.
Analysts said traders knee-jerk reaction has been to buy $10 or $20 million in dollar/mark so the market has found itself caught slightly long.
This means there is a good chance of a pull-back to perhaps the 1.4860 mark area before it begins to move higher again.
Oil prices spiked, with Brent touching $23.50 a barrel, and if they stay high it will start to hit the yen as Japan imports all its oil. But petro-currencies will obviously benefit.

"As is usual in times of increased international tension, a generally dollar positive tone has been set, particularly against the yen, as the Japanese economy's exposure to higher oil prices depresses any yen positive sentiment," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered. Traders also said a Wall Street Journal article hinting at an imminent Fed rate rise helped boost the dollar.

The article said Fed policy makers are moving towards a sharper than expected increase in interest rates unless clear signs of slower growth appear in the next three weeks. The next FOMC meeting is on September 24.

The Wall Street Journal article put the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index into sharp focus, paticularly after last week's much stronger than expected Chicago PMI. Friday's jobs data will also be crucial.

A Reuter survey expected the August NAPM index up at 52.9 after 50.2 in July, but the risk is of a higher figure after the strong Chicago PMI, analysts said. But the U.S. strike on Iraq was the main talking point. The U.S. raid was in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds in the north. U.S. defence officials said unmanned Cruise missiles were fired at "selected air defence targets."
Analysts said for the dollar to continue to benefit from the renewed Middle East problems, there will have to be an escalation of the tension.
"If we were to see significantly higher oil prices and therefore some further selling of the yen the dollar may be helped higher all round," Banque Paribas' Parsons said.
When U.S. forex traders arrive at their desks there could be a further wave of dollar buying, analysts said.
President Clinton will make a formal statement on the strike at 1200 GMT and that could well spark some further U.S. dollar buying interest.
In later trade the dollar settled at 1.4888/92 marks and 109.30/40 yen as the market awaited further developments and the U.S. opening.
"We had been expecting intervention, we didn't expect it to be military intervention," said one trader who had been anticipating some central bank action to boost the dollar this week.
